title: Embers night surge play
content:
Quick personal runbook / scratchpad for late-night GPU surge events. Purpose: capture the things I do/think about when the queue spikes unexpectedly and I need to triage capacity/network/GPU stalls quickly. Not polished — notes to self.

TL;DR checklist (for me):
- Check queue backlog (torque/queue dashboard) + per-pool latency heatmap -> where is the hotspot?
- Confirm whether surge is traffic (hosted) or internal replication/job churn (dedicated/private)
- If >30% preemptions or OOMs: check node metrics and spot/interrupt logs
- If model-level slowdowns: fall back to smaller quantized variant & enable KV prefix cache for hot clients
- Communicate to #infra-oncall + @Maya if ETA > 30m

Immediate commands to run (copy-paste):
- curl -s 'https://console.internal/queues/api/backlog?pool=all' | jq .summary
- kubectl --context prod-gpu get pods -n infra -o wide | grep serving
- klogs=$(kubectl -n infra logs -l app=serving-runtime --tail=200) && echo "$klogs" | rg "OOM|preempt|failed to allocate" -n
- gcloud compute instances list --filter="labels=redwood-pool" --format="table(name,status,cpuPlatform,zone)"

Observations I often miss:
- Network windows: a transient Azure/Cloud GW route flap shows up as 5-10s RT spikes across many pods — look at node.dmesg and cloud provider status page before draining nodes.
- Autoscaler cooldowns: when we bounce many nodes at once, the autoscaler can hit rate limits; prefer staggered scale-ups (5 nodes every 2m) for large pools.
- Batching effects: increasing batch_size can reduce token cost but increase tail latency; for immediate surge, bias to smaller batch_size and faster preemption.

Short checklist: triage -> mitigate -> communicate -> followup
1) Triage (5–10m):
   - backlog by route (api/embeddings vs api/generate)
   - per-tenant telemetry: top 3 tenants causing spike (console filters)
   - GPU memory pressure: nvidia-smi summary on suspect nodes
2) Mitigate (10–30m):
   - soft-mitigations: enable per-route rate limits, reduce max_tokens for streaming routes, switch noisy tenant to slower model variant
   - node actions: cordon -> drain (kubectl cordon <node> && kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force) but hold if GPU jobs are long-running and a partial fallback path exists
   - routing: rotate traffic to dedicated pools in different region (if cross-region fallback policy is allowed)
3) Communicate:
   - post short note to #infra-oncall: cause, immediate step taken, ETA estimate, P0 owners tagged
4) Followups (post-mortem items):
   - add a targeted eval for the noisy tenant on Redwood Optimize to detect regressions early; track token-per-second and tail latency in the dashboard
   - consider pre-warming additional small instance types for predictable nightly jobs

Quick notes / heuristics:
- If 1–2 nodes show repeated nvml errors -> likely kernel or driver mismatch; escalate to infra-image team (link image build PR in slack thread)
- If preemptions jump but overall node memory pressure low -> suspect scheduler churn (check kube-scheduler logs + API server audit latencies)
- If embedded model stalls (KV cache thrash) -> temporarily disable long prefix caching for that model and let requests hit runtime (recalculate per-route cache TTLs)

Immediate todo items (short term, this doc):
- [ ] Add a canned script in /ops/bin called ember-triage.sh that runs the immediate commands and summarizes (owner: me).
- [ ] Add a Grafana panel that shows Preemptions / Node OOM / Pod Kill count aligned to queue backlog (owner: Samir).
- [ ] Draft a short runbook snippet for the Console Rollouts page describing fallback to quantized variant (owner: Maya).

Questions I want to remember to ask in retrospective:
- Is there a clean SLA-based ordering for dedicated vs hosted routing when capacity is constrained? (current routing fallbacks are heuristics)
- Can we make autoscaler ramp rules add jitter by default to avoid synchronized scale-ups?

Potential quick hacks (use only if we can't scale quickly):
- Enable short-lived token-bucket throttles for noisy tenants (console -> routing -> per-tenant overrides)
- Lower default batch_size in the serving config via feature flag for the next 20m window
- Force roll to a model with smaller KV footprint for routes hitting >1s median per-token compute

Slack snippets I usually paste: 
- "Heads-up: investigating GPU backlog in prod-us-east-1. Currently isolating to pool=high-memory; preemptions at 12%. Mitigations: soft rate-limits for noisy tenant xyz, cordoned 2 nodes for live triage. ETA 25m. @oncall @Maya"

Logs / links I always check quickly:
- /dashboards/queue-backlog (console)
- /dashboards/node-health (grafana)
- /jobs/nightly (airflow) for any big scheduled runs at midnight
- provider status page (e.g., cloud.health.status/ regions)

Random heuristics I've learned:
- Nighttime batch jobs often win the token economy but lose crowd control — if we can shift heavy non-latency workloads to a reserved off-peak window, net tail latency improves.
- Small instance types (v100x2-ish) warm faster for small bursts than big 8x GPU machines — sometimes cheaper to spin a set of small nodes as a hot pool. Experiment with burst pool config.

Notes to self for followups (longer term backlog):
- Evaluate a staged fallback policy that first reduces model size, then reduces batch size, then reduces concurrency — ordered by quality impact.
- Add more anomaly detectors to Redwood Optimize for per-tenant token-rate drift.
- Write a one-pager on autoscaler jitter and recommended defaults for infra teams.

End of scribble. If I wake up to this again, start with the TL;DR checklist above and iterate.

-- Avery
